_readme: TurfScore = sum of weight * factor (each factor 0-1). Weights should total 100. Tune these from field results, not from code.

targeting._readme: Filters a rep can mix and match on the map. Picking none in a group means any. Heating oil uses the ACS share of homes heated with oil (B25040); picking several oil bands uses the lowest one. oil_focus is the one-tap preset; oil_color_breaks are the edges of the five map colors when coloring by oil. Home age uses the median year built of 1-4 family lots in NYC (PLUTO), else ACS B25035; walk lists filter each house by its own year. A tract is flagged renter-heavy when renter-occupied households are at least renter_heavy_share. Homeowner age uses ACS B25007 brackets (15-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-74, 75-84, 85+), so band edges must fall on those. House size uses building square feet where NYC lot data exists, otherwise ACS median rooms. Retired households = share of households with retirement income (pension, 401k/IRA payouts; ACS B19059); picking several retired bands uses the lowest one. The card also shows the share with Social Security (B19055). Voting = 2020 presidential vote by precinct (sources.json → elections), spread over tracts by area; a tract needs vote_min_votes votes to show it; picking several vote bands uses the lowest one. Neighborhood level only, never a household.

people._readme: Neighborhood facts from the Census ACS, per tract, never per house. Languages: B16001 (detailed) or C16001; a language is listed on the tract card when at least language_list_min_share of residents (age 5+) speak it at home, and the Target filter 'Language at home' keeps tracts where a picked language is at least language_filter_min_share. language_filter_choices = how many languages the filter offers (the most spoken across the turf). Born abroad: B05006 place of birth; the card lists up to birthplace_max countries with at least birthplace_min_share of residents. The race / Hispanic mix (B03002) is shown on the card for background only and is never used in the TurfScore or any filter. names renames a Census label for display. When the detailed table isn't published for tracts the map uses C16001, which groups South Asian and many European languages together as 'Other Indo-European languages'.

li_property_classes._readme: NYS assessment property classes kept for Long Island walk lists, and how many homes (units) each means. 21x one-family (215 has an accessory apartment), 220 two-family, 230 three-family, 24x/25x rural residence / estate, 280-283 multiple residences / residence with incidental commercial use. Seasonal (260) and mobile homes (270) are left out.

personal._readme: Each rep's personal turf map ("My fit"), learned from their own knocks and appointments (supabase/008 rep_tract_results). For every tract trait below, the rep's appointments per 100 doors and closes per appointment are compared with their own overall rates; small samples are pulled toward the team's pattern (smooth_doors, smooth_appts). My fit = TurfScore × the rep's average lift over the tract's traits (clamped to multiplier_min..max). Blend: appointment rate counts appt_weight; close rate counts close_weight, phased in as the rep reaches close_full_at appointments. A rep is still 'learning' until min_doors. Tracts another rep claimed, or knocked within recent_days, are flagged so reps don't double-knock. Reasons show only for traits with at least reason_min_doors doors and a lift beyond reason_lift. bins: edges used to group tracts by oil share (low / some / high), retired share, Democratic vote share (R-lean / mixed / D-lean) and the main non-English language (spoken by at least language_min).

financing._readme: Financing-ready (Low / Medium / High): a neighborhood stand-in for credit, since real credit scores by area aren't free and individual scores are off-limits. For each tract: the share of mortgage applications approved and the share denied for credit history (HMDA, owner-occupied 1-4 family homes), and the share of owner homes with no mortgage (ACS B25081). Rates are pulled toward the county's until a tract has min_apps applications. Each part becomes a turf-wide percentile (credit denials counted in reverse), weighted together, and the result split into levels (thirds by default). A tract needs at least min_parts parts. Shown as a Target filter and a card line only: it is NOT part of the TurfScore.
